src: Serious Eats — Sasha Marx — "Traditional Duck Confit"

time.en: 10 min | Cook: 245 min | Total: 1695 min

en.v: Food processor, 2840 ml stainless steel saucier, rimmed baking sheet

sk.v: Kuchynský robot, nerezová rajnica s guľatým dnom (saucier) 2840 ml, plech s okrajom

en.v: Duck confit can be refrigerated in an airtight opaque container, with legs completely submerged in fat, for up to 1 month. The duck fat from the confit can be reused at least 2 more times for subsequent batches of confit; after the third use, taste it for salinity as it will eventually become too salty

sk.v: Kačacie confit môžeme uchovávať v chladničke v uzatvárateľnej nepriehľadnej nádobe so stehnami úplne ponorenými v tuku až 1 mesiac. Kačaciu masť z confitu môžeme použiť ešte najmenej 2-krát na ďalšie dávky confitu; po treťom použití ju ochutnáme, či nie je príliš slaná, lebo časom zosolí

c.t: Works with all duck breeds (developed with Pekin and Alina ducks). Without a spare onion for the cure, use 3 to 4 more shallots.

The amount of duck fat depends on the size of the vessel: the legs must stay fully covered throughout cooking. Render it yourself or buy it in well-stocked supermarkets or online. The recipe scales up or down, but the fat-to-duck ratio changes with the vessel.
Funguje so všetkými plemenami kačíc (recept bol vyvinutý s pekinskými kačicami a plemenom Alina). Ak nemáte cibuľu na nasolenie, použite o 3 až 4 šalotky viac.

Množstvo kačacej masti závisí od veľkosti nádoby: stehná musia byť počas celého varenia úplne ponorené. Masť si vyškvarte sami alebo ju kúpte v dobre zásobenom supermarkete či online. Recept sa dá zväčšiť aj zmenšiť, ale pomer masti a mäsa sa mení s nádobou.

en.t: 4 duck legs (about 1000 g total)
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp (16 g) Diamond Crystal kosher salt; for table salt, use about half as much by volume or the same weight
6 large shallots (340 g), quartered
1 small onion (110 g), cut into 5 cm pieces
6 medium cloves garlic (30 g)
1/2 bunch (55 g) flat-leaf parsley leaves and tender stems, roughly chopped
10 sprigs fresh thyme
2 tsp (6 g) whole black peppercorns
475 to 950 ml rendered duck fat

sk.t: 4 kačacie stehná (spolu asi 1000 g)
1 PL a 1 ČL (16 g) hrubozrnná soľ Diamond Crystal (pri jemnej soli asi objemovo polovica alebo rovnaká hmotnosť)
6 veľkých šalotiek (340 g), rozštvrtené
1 malá cibuľa (110 g), nakrájaná na 5 cm kúsky
6 stredných strúčikov cesnaku (30 g)
lístky a mäkké stonky hladkolistej petržlenovej vňate (½ zväzkov (55 g)), nahrubo nasekané
čerstvý tymián (10 vetvičiek)
2 ČL (6 g) celé čierne korenie
475 až 950 ml vyškvarená kačacia masť

en.t: 1. The Day Before Cooking Confit: Season duck legs evenly on all sides with salt; set aside. Combine shallots, onion, garlic, and parsley in food processor bowl and pulse until finely chopped but not puréed, about 15 pulses.

2. Transfer half the vegetable mixture to a nonreactive container that can fit duck legs snugly, such as a baking dish, and spread in an even layer. Scatter half the thyme sprigs and peppercorns over vegetable mixture, then arrange duck legs skin-side up in an even layer on top, pressing them into vegetable mixture. Distribute remaining thyme sprigs and peppercorns over duck legs, followed by the vegetable mixture, spreading it evenly so legs are well-coated. Cover tightly with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 24 hours and up to 48 hours. Alternatively, combine duck legs, vegetable mixture, thyme, and peppercorns in a 3790 ml zipper-lock bag. Seal bag, pressing out as much air as possible. Massage bag until duck legs are evenly coated on all sides. Lay bag flat on rimmed baking sheet and refrigerate for at least 24 hours and up to 48 hours.

3. When Ready to Cook: Adjust oven rack to middle position and preheat oven to 105 °C (fan 85 °C). Melt duck fat, either in 2840 ml saucier over low heat or in a microwave-safe bowl in the microwave. Remove duck legs from cure, wiping away as much of the cure mixture as possible before rinsing legs gently under cold water to remove all seasonings; discard cure. Pat duck legs dry with paper towels, then arrange in single layer in saucier with duck fat (if using), making sure they are completely submerged in fat. Alternatively, arrange duck legs snugly in a small baking dish and cover with melted duck fat, making sure legs are fully submerged in fat.

4. Cover saucier or baking dish with lid or aluminum foil, and transfer to oven. Cook until duck is completely tender and meat shows almost no resistance when pierced with a paring knife, and skin has begun to pull away from bottom of the drumstick, 3 1/2 to 4 hours.

5. Remove from oven and cool duck to room temperature in its cooking vessel, removing lid but keeping it submerged in fat. Once cool, cover container tightly and transfer to refrigerator, where confit can be stored for up to 1 month.

sk.t: 1. Deň pred prípravou confitu: kačacie stehná zo všetkých strán rovnomerne osolíme; odložíme. V nádobe kuchynského robota spojíme šalotku, cibuľu, cesnak a petržlenovú vňať a pulzne nasekáme nadrobno, ale nie na pyré, asi 15 pulzov.

2. Polovicu zeleninovej zmesi preložíme do nereaktívnej nádoby, do ktorej sa stehná tesne zmestia, napríklad do zapekacej misy, a rozotrieme v rovnomernej vrstve. Na zeleninovú zmes rozložíme polovicu vetvičiek tymiánu a zrniek korenia, potom navrch poukladáme kačacie stehná kožou nahor v rovnomernej vrstve a vtlačíme ich do zeleninovej zmesi. Na stehná rozložíme zvyšný tymián a korenie a potom zvyšnú zeleninovú zmes, ktorú rovnomerne rozotrieme, aby boli stehná dobre pokryté. Tesne prikryjeme potravinovou fóliou a necháme v chladničke aspoň 24 hodín a najviac 48 hodín. Prípadne kačacie stehná, zeleninovú zmes, tymián a korenie vložíme do 3,79-litrového uzatvárateľného vrecka. Vrecko uzavrieme a vytlačíme čo najviac vzduchu. Vrecko premasírujeme, kým nie sú stehná zo všetkých strán rovnomerne obalené. Vrecko položíme naplocho na plech s okrajom a necháme v chladničke aspoň 24 hodín a najviac 48 hodín.

3. Keď sme pripravení variť: rošt v rúre posunieme do strednej polohy a rúru rozohrejeme na 105 °C (teplovzdušnú na 85 °C). Kačací tuk roztopíme buď v 2,84-litrovom kastróliku (saucier) na miernom ohni, alebo v mise vhodnej do mikrovlnnej rúry v mikrovlnke. Kačacie stehná vyberieme z nakladacej zmesi, zotrieme z nich čo najviac zmesi a potom ich jemne opláchneme pod studenou vodou, aby sme odstránili všetko korenie; nakladaciu zmes vyhodíme. Stehná osušíme papierovými utierkami a poukladáme v jednej vrstve do kastróla s kačacím tukom (ak ho používame) tak, aby boli úplne ponorené v tuku. Prípadne stehná tesne poukladáme do malej zapekacej misy a zalejeme roztopeným kačacím tukom tak, aby boli úplne ponorené.

4. Kastról alebo zapekaciu misu prikryjeme pokrievkou alebo alobalom a vložíme do rúry. Pečieme, kým kačica nie je úplne mäkká, mäso pri prepichnutí malým nožom takmer neodoláva a koža sa začala odťahovať od spodku paličky, 3 1/2 až 4 hodiny.

5. Vyberieme z rúry a kačicu necháme vychladnúť na izbovú teplotu v nádobe, v ktorej sa piekla; pokrievku odstránime, ale kačica zostane ponorená v tuku. Po vychladnutí nádobu tesne prikryjeme a preložíme do chladničky, kde confit vydrží až 1 mesiac.

3. Keď sme pripravení variť: rošt v rúre posunieme do strednej polohy a rúru rozohrejeme na 105 °C (teplovzdušnú na 85 °C). Kačací tuk roztopíme buď v 2,84-litrovom kastróliku (saucier) na miernom ohni, alebo v mise vhodnej do mikrovlnnej rúry v mikrovlnke. Kačacie stehná vyberieme z nakladacej zmesi, zotrieme z nich čo najviac zmesi a potom ich jemne opláchneme pod studenou vodou, aby sme odstránili všetko korenie; nakladaciu zmes vyhodíme. Stehná osušíme papierovými utierkami a poukladáme v jednej vrstve do kastróla s kačacím tukom (ak ho používame) tak, aby boli úplne ponorené v tuku. Prípadne stehná tesne poukladáme do malej zapekacej misy a zalejeme roztopeným kačacím tukom tak, aby boli úplne ponorené.

4. Kastról alebo zapekaciu misu prikryjeme pokrievkou alebo alobalom a vložíme do rúry. Pečieme, kým kačica nie je úplne mäkká, mäso pri prepichnutí malým nožom takmer neodoláva a koža sa začala odťahovať od spodku paličky, 3 1/2 až 4 hodiny.

5. Vyberieme z rúry a kačicu necháme vychladnúť na izbovú teplotu v nádobe, v ktorej sa piekla; pokrievku odstránime, ale kačica zostane ponorená v tuku. Po vychladnutí nádobu tesne prikryjeme a preložíme do chladničky, kde confit vydrží až 1 mesiac.

en.t: 1. On a very clean work surface and using a sharp knife, slice beef into thin slices no thicker than 0.5 cm. Then cut into thin 3 mm or 0.5 cm strips. Cut strips crosswise into a fine mince. Transfer to a mixing bowl.

2. Add mayonnaise and season with salt and pepper to taste, stirring well to combine thoroughly. If needed add additional olive oil, vinegar, and/or mustard in very small increments to adjust flavor to taste (depending on your mayonnaise, you may not need any, or you may find the beef needs a little more to get the flavor just right). If desired, mix in the drops of fish sauce.
3. Add shallot, chives, parsley, cornichon, and capers and stir until thoroughly combined.

4. Mound steak tartare on a serving plate (you can use a ring mold to make a perfect circle, if desired). Top with egg yolk, if using, and serve right away with toasts and additional cornichons on the side.

sk.t: 1. Na veľmi čistej pracovnej ploche ostrým nožom nakrájame hovädzie mäso na tenké plátky hrubé najviac 0,5 cm. Potom ich nakrájame na tenké prúžky široké 3 mm alebo 0,5 cm. Prúžky nakrájame naprieč najemno. Preložíme do misy.

2. Pridáme majonézu, osolíme a okoreníme podľa chuti a dôkladne premiešame. Ak treba, po veľmi malých dávkach pridáme ďalší olivový olej, ocot a/alebo horčicu, aby sme chuť doladili (podľa majonézy nemusíme pridávať nič, alebo zistíme, že mäso potrebuje trochu viac, aby chuť bola akurát). Podľa chuti primiešame kvapky rybacej omáčky.
3. Pridáme šalotku, pažítku, petržlenovú vňať, kyslé uhorky (cornichons) a kapary a dôkladne premiešame.
4. Tatarák navŕšime na servírovací tanier (ak chceme dokonalý kruh, môžeme použiť krúžok). Navrch dáme žĺtok, ak ho používame, a hneď podávame s hrienkami a ďalšími kyslými uhorkami nabok.

en.t: 2 T-bone steaks or porterhouse steaks, each 4 cm thick (about 1590 g total), patted dry
1 clove garlic, halved
2 tsp (6 g) kosher salt
1 tsp (5 ml) ground black pepper
3 tbsp (44 ml) extra-virgin olive oil
Lemon wedges for serving
1. **IF USING A CHARCOAL GRILL:**

2. Light large chimney starter filled with hardwood charcoal (about 1130 g) and burn until covered with layer of fine gray ash. Build two-level fire by stacking most of the coals on one side of grill and arranging remaining coals in single layer on other side. Set cooking grate in place, cover grill with lid, and let grate heat up, about 5 minutes. Use wire brush to scrape grate clean. Grill is ready when thicker layer of coals is medium-hot (you can hold your hand 13 cm above cooking grate for 3 to 4 seconds).
3. **IF USING A GAS GRILL:**

4. Turn all burners on gas grill to high, close lid, and heat until very hot, about 15 minutes. Scrape cooking grate clean with wire brush; leave one burner on high and turn other burner(s) down to medium.

5. Meanwhile, rub halved garlic clove over bone and meat on each side of steak, and then sprinkle the steaks evenly on both sides with salt and pepper. Cook steaks, uncovered, over hotter part of grill until well-browned on each side, about 2 1/2 minutes per side. (If steaks start to flame, move them to cooler side of fire and/or extinguish flames with squirt bottle). Move steaks to cooler side of grill and continue cooking, turning once, to desired doneness, 5 to 6 minutes more for rare (50 °C on instant-read thermometer), 6 to 7 minutes for rare medium-rare (50 °C), 7 to 8 minutes for medium medium-rare (55 °C), or 8 to 9 minutes for medium (55 to 60 °C).

6. Transfer steaks to cutting board and let rest 5 minutes. Cut strip and tenderloin pieces off bones and slice crosswise about 1.5 cm thick. Arrange slices on platter, drizzle with olive oil, and serve immediately with lemon wedges.

1. **AK POUŽÍVAME GRIL NA DREVENÉ UHLIE:**

2. Zapálime veľký komín (podpaľovač) naplnený dreveným uhlím z tvrdého dreva (asi 1130 g) a necháme horieť, kým uhlie nepokryje vrstva jemného sivého popola. Vložíme grilovací rošt, gril prikryjeme vekom a necháme rošt rozohriať, asi 5 minút. Rošt očistíme drôtenou kefou. Gril je pripravený, keď je hrubšia vrstva uhlia stredne horúca (ruku udržíme 13 cm nad roštom 3 až 4 sekundy).
3. **AK POUŽÍVAME PLYNOVÝ GRIL:**

time.en: 5 min | Cook: 20 min | Total: 25 min

c.t: Ají amarillo peppers are fruity, floral and quite hot; Latin groceries often sell them frozen. A similar amount of red bell pepper plus jalapeño can be used instead.
Papričky ají amarillo sú ovocné, kvetinové a dosť pálivé; latinskoamerické obchody ich často predávajú mrazené. Namiesto nich môžete použiť podobné množstvo červenej papriky a jalapeña.

en.t: 450 g beef tenderloin, skirt steak, or other tender and flavorful quick-cooking steak
60 ml peanut, canola, or vegetable oil, divided, plus more if needed
Kosher salt
1 medium (225 g) red onion, cut into 1.5 cm slices
4 scallions (about 60 g total), roots and any wilted parts trimmed, remainder cut into 5 cm lengths
1 fresh or frozen ají amarillo chili pepper (about 60 g), defrosted if frozen, then stemmed, seeded, and sliced lengthwise into matchsticks
2 medium plum tomatoes (about 160 g total), cored and cut into 2 cm-thick wedges
2 medium cloves garlic, minced
2.5 cm piece peeled fresh ginger (about 7 g), minced
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp (20 ml) soy sauce
1 tbsp (15 ml) apple cider vinegar
2 tsp (10 ml) minced fresh cilantro leaves and tender stems
Freshly ground black pepper
French fries, for serving
Cooked long-grain rice, for serving
1. Cut the beef across the grain into roughly 1.5 cm-thick strips.
2. In a wok or large cast iron or stainless steel skillet, heat 2 tbsp (30 ml) oil over high heat until heavily smoking. Meanwhile, season beef all over with salt.

3. Working in batches, add just enough beef to the pan to sear it heavily without steaming in its own juices. Spread the beef around so the pieces are evenly spaced apart and allow to cook until very well seared and charred on one side, 30 seconds to 1 minute. Stir and toss beef so that it cooks all over, about 30 seconds longer; if you are working over a gas flame and aren't afraid of some fire, toss the beef near the flame so that the oil briefly combusts in big bursts. (If this makes you nervous, don't allow it to catch fire. Instead, manage the heat to prevent flare-ups.) Using a spatula, transfer beef to a platter to rest. Repeat with remaining beef, always getting the pan smoking-hot before the next batch and adding more oil if needed.

4. When all the beef is cooked, return the empty pan to high heat. Add 1 tbsp (15 ml) oil and heat until smoking. Working in batches, add just enough red onion so that it sears and browns rapidly without steaming, about 30 seconds. Toss a few times until the onion is crisp-tender. Using a spatula, transfer onion to a platter. Repeat with remaining onion, always heating the pan until smoking first and adding more oil if necessary.

5. Return the empty pan to high heat, add 1 tbsp (15 ml) oil, and heat until smoking. Working in batches if necessary, add scallions and cook, without stirring, until seared on bottom side, about 30 seconds. Push scallions to the side and add peppers. Cook until seared, about 30 seconds longer.

6. Push scallions and peppers to the side and add tomatoes to the pan, allowing them to sear on one side, about 30 seconds. (If your burner isn't very strong, you can remove the scallions and peppers from the pan before adding the tomatoes to guarantee good searing. Otherwise, leave them in.) Try not to let the tomatoes grow too soft and pulpy; it's better that they retain their shape rather than brown to the point of becoming mushy.
7. Add garlic and ginger and cook, tossing and stirring constantly, until lightly sautéed and fragrant, about 15 seconds. Add soy sauce and vinegar and toss to combine.

8. Return beef and all accumulated juices to the pan along with the red onions. (If you've removed the scallions and peppers, add them back now, too.) Add cilantro. Toss over high heat to combine well, seasoning with salt and pepper as you go. Remove from heat.
9. Spoon stir-fry onto plates with a mound of cooked rice and French fries and serve right away.

c.t: 1. Cut the beef across the grain into roughly 1.5 cm-thick strips.
2. In a wok or large cast iron or stainless steel skillet, heat 1¼ tbsp (18 ml) oil over high heat until heavily smoking. Meanwhile, season beef all over with salt.

3. Working in batches, add just enough beef to the pan to sear it heavily without steaming in its own juices. Spread the beef around so the pieces are evenly spaced apart and allow to cook until very well seared and charred on one side, 30 seconds to 1 minute. Stir and toss beef so that it cooks all over, about 30 seconds longer; if you are working over a gas flame and aren't afraid of some fire, toss the beef near the flame so that the oil briefly combusts in big bursts. (If this makes you nervous, don't allow it to catch fire. Instead, manage the heat to prevent flare-ups.) Using a spatula, transfer beef to a platter to rest. Repeat with remaining beef, always getting the pan smoking-hot before the next batch and adding more oil if needed.

4. When all the beef is cooked, return the empty pan to high heat. Add 1¾ tsp (9 ml) oil and heat until smoking. Working in batches, add just enough red onion so that it sears and browns rapidly without steaming, about 30 seconds. Toss a few times until the onion is crisp-tender. Using a spatula, transfer onion to a platter. Repeat with remaining onion, always heating the pan until smoking first and adding more oil if necessary.

5. Return the empty pan to high heat, add 1¾ tsp (9 ml) oil, and heat until smoking. Working in batches if necessary, add scallions and cook, without stirring, until seared on bottom side, about 30 seconds. Push scallions to the side and add peppers. Cook until seared, about 30 seconds longer.

6. Push scallions and peppers to the side and add tomatoes to the pan, allowing them to sear on one side, about 30 seconds. (If your burner isn't very strong, you can remove the scallions and peppers from the pan before adding the tomatoes to guarantee good searing. Otherwise, leave them in.) Try not to let the tomatoes grow too soft and pulpy; it's better that they retain their shape rather than brown to the point of becoming mushy.
7. Add garlic and ginger and cook, tossing and stirring constantly, until lightly sautéed and fragrant, about 15 seconds. Add soy sauce and vinegar and toss to combine.

8. Return beef and all accumulated juices to the pan along with the red onions. (If you've removed the scallions and peppers, add them back now, too.) Add cilantro. Toss over high heat to combine well, seasoning with salt and pepper as you go. Remove from heat.
9. Spoon stir-fry onto plates with a mound of cooked rice and French fries and serve right away.
1. Hovädzie mäso nakrájame naprieč vláknami na prúžky hrubé zhruba 1,5 cm.
2. Vo woku alebo veľkej liatinovej či nerezovej panvici rozpálime na silnom ohni 1¼ PL (18 ml) oleja, kým silno nedymí. Medzitým mäso zo všetkých strán osolíme.

3. Po dávkach pridávame do panvice len toľko mäsa, aby sa intenzívne opieklo a nedusilo sa vo vlastnej šťave. Mäso rozložíme tak, aby boli kúsky rovnomerne od seba, a necháme ho, kým nie je z jednej strany veľmi dobre opečené a pripálené, 30 sekúnd až 1 minútu. Mäso premiešame a prehodíme, aby sa opieklo zo všetkých strán, ešte asi 30 sekúnd; ak varíme na plynovom plameni a nebojíme sa ohňa, mäso prehadzujeme blízko plameňa, aby olej nakrátko vzbĺkol vo veľkých záblesoch. (Ak nás to znervózňuje, nenecháme ho vzbĺknuť. Namiesto toho reguláciou ohňa zabránime vzplanutiu.) Obracačkou preložíme mäso na tanier, aby odpočívalo. Zopakujeme so zvyšným mäsom; pred každou ďalšou dávkou panvicu vždy rozpálime, kým nedymí, a ak treba, prilejeme olej.

4. Keď je všetko mäso hotové, prázdnu panvicu vrátime na silný oheň. Pridáme 1¾ ČL (9 ml) oleja a rozpálime, kým nedymí. Po dávkach pridávame len toľko červenej cibule, aby sa rýchlo opiekla a zhnedla bez dusenia, asi 30 sekúnd. Niekoľkokrát prehodíme, kým cibuľa nie je mäkká, ale ešte chrumkavá. Obracačkou preložíme cibuľu na tanier. Zopakujeme so zvyšnou cibuľou; panvicu vždy najprv rozpálime, kým nedymí, a ak treba, prilejeme olej.

5. Prázdnu panvicu vrátime na silný oheň, pridáme 1¾ ČL (9 ml) oleja a rozpálime, kým nedymí. Podľa potreby po dávkach pridáme jarnú cibuľku a bez miešania opekáme, kým nie je zospodu opečená, asi 30 sekúnd. Jarnú cibuľku odsunieme nabok a pridáme papričky. Opekáme, kým sa neopečú, ešte asi 30 sekúnd.

6. Jarnú cibuľku a papričky odsunieme nabok, do panvice pridáme paradajky a necháme ich z jednej strany opiecť, asi 30 sekúnd. (Ak horák nie je veľmi silný, môžeme jarnú cibuľku a papričky pred pridaním paradajok z panvice vybrať, aby sa paradajky určite dobre opiekli. Inak ich necháme v panvici.) Snažíme sa, aby paradajky príliš nezmäkli a nerozpadli sa; je lepšie, keď si zachovajú tvar, než aby zhnedli až do kašovitej konzistencie.
7. Pridáme cesnak a zázvor a za stáleho prehadzovania a miešania opekáme, kým sa zľahka neopražia a nezavoňajú, asi 15 sekúnd. Pridáme sójovú omáčku a ocot a premiešame.

8. Do panvice vrátime mäso so všetkou nazbieranou šťavou spolu s červenou cibuľou. (Ak sme vybrali jarnú cibuľku a papričky, teraz ich tiež vrátime.) Pridáme koriandrovú vňať. Na silnom ohni dobre premiešame a priebežne dochucujeme soľou a korením. Odstavíme z ohňa.
9. Zmes naberieme na taniere s kôpkou uvarenej ryže a hranolčekmi a hneď podávame.

en.v: Steps 3-7 of the recipe can easily be done a day or two ahead of time. Store the resulting partially cooked meat in an airtight container in the refrigerator. Steps 8 and 10 can also be done a day or two ahead of time. Store the fully fried herb mixture in an airtight container in the refrigerator. Like many other Persian khoreshes, ghormeh-sabzi can be made a day or two ahead of time as long as it is reheated gently.

sk.v: Kroky 3-7 receptu môžeme ľahko urobiť deň či dva vopred. Čiastočne uvarené mäso uchovávame v uzatvárateľnej nádobe v chladničke. Aj kroky 8 a 10 môžeme urobiť deň či dva vopred. Úplne opraženú bylinkovú zmes uchovávame v uzatvárateľnej nádobe v chladničke. Ako mnohé iné perzské khoreše, aj ghormeh-sabzi môžeme pripraviť deň či dva vopred, ak ho jemne ohrejeme.

c.t: Canned beans can replace the dried beans: add them during the last 30 minutes of cooking. Some Persian, Afghan and Middle Eastern markets sell frozen or dried ready-mixed ghormeh sabzi herbs.

Sušenú fazuľu môžete nahradiť sterilizovanou: pridajte ju až počas posledných 30 minút varenia. Niektoré perzské, afganské a blízkovýchodné obchody predávajú mrazenú alebo sušenú hotovú bylinkovú zmes na ghormeh sabzi.

en.t: 170 g dried red kidney beans
2 tsp (6 g) Diamond Crystal Kosher salt; for table salt use half as much by volume, divided
6 larger or 8 smaller whole dried limes (total weight about 28 g)
120 ml olive oil or ghee, divided
907 g boneless leg of lamb, lamb shoulder, neck or shank, or stewing beef such as beef chuck, short ribs, or oxtail, cut in 2.5–4 cm chunks
1/2 tsp (2.5 ml) freshly ground black pepper
1 medium white or yellow onion (about 226 g), peeled and cut into 0.5 cm dice
1 tsp (5 ml) ground turmeric
125 g fresh cilantro leaves and tender stems
125 g fresh parsley leaves and tender stems
125 g fresh Persian leeks, chives, green parts of scallions, or the middle third section of common leeks
1 tbsp (15 ml) crushed dried fenugreek leaves
1. In a medium bowl, soak red kidney beans in room temperature water to cover by 2.5 cm with 1 tsp (5 ml) of salt for at least 30 minutes or until ready to use.
2. In a separate medium bowl, soak whole Persian dry limes in room temperature water for 30 minutes or until ready to use; place a plate on top of bowl to ensure limes are submerged.

3. Season meat all over with 1 tsp (5 ml) salt and 1/2 tsp (2.5 ml) pepper. In a large Dutch oven or pot, heat 2 tbsp (30 ml) oil or ghee over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add seasoned meat to the saucepan in a single layer. Cook, turning occasionally until meat is well browned on all sides, about 10 minutes. With a slotted spoon, transfer meat to a plate and set aside.
4. Lower heat to medium, and once rendered fat in pan is shimmering, add onions and cook until translucent and edges have turned golden brown, 7 to 10 minutes.
5. Sprinkle 1 tsp (5 ml) turmeric over the sautéed onions, stir thoroughly and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
6. Add 590 ml of water to the saucepan, bring to boil, while scraping the bottom of the saucepan to free up all brown bits left.
7. Add seared meat. Stir to mix, return to boil, then reduce heat to medium low to maintain a simmer; cover and cook for 30 minutes.

8. Meanwhile, prepare the herbs. Wash all fresh herbs and leeks or chives well. Spread over a clean kitchen towel and gently roll to remove excess water. Alternatively, use a salad spinner to achieve the same results.

9. Harvest the leaves and most tender stems from the bundles of parsley and cilantro (If you wish, save the scraps and longer tough stems for other purposes such as making broth.) Chop all fresh herbs (including chives or leeks) as finely as you can. The finer you chop them the more luscious the ghormeh-sabzi will be. Feel free to use a food processor to chop the herbs. However never chop the chives or leeks in the food processor by themselves—if you do, they will turn into an unpleasant mushy mess. Either mix them with the parsley and cilantro to be chopped in the food processor or simply chop them separately the good old fashioned way with a sharp knife on a cutting board.

10. After the meat has cooked for 30 minutes, drain the kidney beans and add to the pot, stir to combine and cover. Adjust the heat so the content of the pot is simmering gently. Cook for another 30 minutes.

11. Meanwhile, in a large frying pan, heat 59 ml ghee or oil over medium-high heat until shimmering. Reduce heat to medium. Add half of the chopped herb mixture. Carefully stir to mix well with oil. Cook until well coated and beginning to cook down, about a minute. Add the rest of the chopped parsley-cilantro-leek mixture. Cook, stirring often until cooked down for 10 minutes, then sprinkle with crushed dried fenugreek leaves. Continue cooking, stirring often, until the herbs are very wilted and are a dark green color but not burned, about 10 more minutes. The herbs are ready when they feel a bit dry but when pressed with the back of a spoon exude shiny bright green oil, and you can smell a strong savory aroma. This is a crucial step that could take 20 to 25 minutes total. Be patient.
12. Drain the whole Persian dried limes. With a sharp instrument (such as a tine of a fork or the tip of a sharp knife), make 6 or 7 small holes in the outer skin of each lime.

13. After the meat has cooked for 1 hour, add the fried herbs and the pierced dried limes to the meat and gently stir. Cover and adjust heat as needed to maintain a gentle simmer and cook, gently stirring every 20 minutes until the meat and beans are tender and the stew is thickened, 60 to 80 minutes.

14. By this time, the whole Persian dry limes should be quite soft, plump, and juicy–full of tangy, sourish, earthy liquid. With a slotted spoon or small strainer, lift one of the whole Persian dry limes and very gently press down on it with the back of a fork without breaking the exterior skin, letting some of the interior liquid drip into the stew. Repeat with another 3 or 4 of the limes. Gently swirl the pot. Taste. If you can’t sense enough of the tangy, sourish, earthy flavor of the limes, repeat with the rest of the limes. It is OK if the exterior skin of the limes breaks in this process—just don’t let the seeds get into the stew as they are a bit bitter if chewed.

15. Season to taste with salt as needed and serve.

c.t: 1. In a medium bowl, soak red kidney beans in room temperature water to cover by 2.5 cm with 1 tsp (5 ml) of salt for at least 30 minutes or until ready to use.
2. In a separate medium bowl, soak whole Persian dry limes in room temperature water for 30 minutes or until ready to use; place a plate on top of bowl to ensure limes are submerged.

3. Season meat all over with 1 tsp (5 ml) salt and 1/2 tsp (2.5 ml) pepper. In a large Dutch oven or pot, heat 1¼ tbsp (18 ml) oil or ghee over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add seasoned meat to the saucepan in a single layer. Cook, turning occasionally until meat is well browned on all sides, about 10 minutes. With a slotted spoon, transfer meat to a plate and set aside.
4. Lower heat to medium, and once rendered fat in pan is shimmering, add onions and cook until translucent and edges have turned golden brown, 7 to 10 minutes.
5. Sprinkle 1 tsp (5 ml) turmeric over the sautéed onions, stir thoroughly and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
6. Add 590 ml of water to the saucepan, bring to boil, while scraping the bottom of the saucepan to free up all brown bits left.
7. Add seared meat. Stir to mix, return to boil, then reduce heat to medium low to maintain a simmer; cover and cook for 30 minutes.

8. Meanwhile, prepare the herbs. Wash all fresh herbs and leeks or chives well. Spread over a clean kitchen towel and gently roll to remove excess water. Alternatively, use a salad spinner to achieve the same results.

9. Harvest the leaves and most tender stems from the bundles of parsley and cilantro (If you wish, save the scraps and longer tough stems for other purposes such as making broth.) Chop all fresh herbs (including chives or leeks) as finely as you can. The finer you chop them the more luscious the ghormeh-sabzi will be. Feel free to use a food processor to chop the herbs. However never chop the chives or leeks in the food processor by themselves—if you do, they will turn into an unpleasant mushy mess. Either mix them with the parsley and cilantro to be chopped in the food processor or simply chop them separately the good old fashioned way with a sharp knife on a cutting board.

10. After the meat has cooked for 30 minutes, drain the kidney beans and add to the pot, stir to combine and cover. Adjust the heat so the content of the pot is simmering gently. Cook for another 30 minutes.

11. Meanwhile, in a large frying pan, heat 35 ml ghee or oil over medium-high heat until shimmering. Reduce heat to medium. Add half of the chopped herb mixture. Carefully stir to mix well with oil. Cook until well coated and beginning to cook down, about a minute. Add the rest of the chopped parsley-cilantro-leek mixture. Cook, stirring often until cooked down for 10 minutes, then sprinkle with crushed dried fenugreek leaves. Continue cooking, stirring often, until the herbs are very wilted and are a dark green color but not burned, about 10 more minutes. The herbs are ready when they feel a bit dry but when pressed with the back of a spoon exude shiny bright green oil, and you can smell a strong savory aroma. This is a crucial step that could take 20 to 25 minutes total. Be patient.
12. Drain the whole Persian dried limes. With a sharp instrument (such as a tine of a fork or the tip of a sharp knife), make 6 or 7 small holes in the outer skin of each lime.

13. After the meat has cooked for 1 hour, add the fried herbs and the pierced dried limes to the meat and gently stir. Cover and adjust heat as needed to maintain a gentle simmer and cook, gently stirring every 20 minutes until the meat and beans are tender and the stew is thickened, 60 to 80 minutes.

14. By this time, the whole Persian dry limes should be quite soft, plump, and juicy–full of tangy, sourish, earthy liquid. With a slotted spoon or small strainer, lift one of the whole Persian dry limes and very gently press down on it with the back of a fork without breaking the exterior skin, letting some of the interior liquid drip into the stew. Repeat with another 3 or 4 of the limes. Gently swirl the pot. Taste. If you can’t sense enough of the tangy, sourish, earthy flavor of the limes, repeat with the rest of the limes. It is OK if the exterior skin of the limes breaks in this process—just don’t let the seeds get into the stew as they are a bit bitter if chewed.

15. When ready, ghormeh-sabzi should be quite thick, be a very dark green color with red kidney beans, chunks of tender meat, and the limes poking out of the sea of the green herbs, tasting noticeably tangy, with the unique aroma of cooked fenugreek having filled the kitchen. Season to taste with salt as needed and serve.
1. V strednej mise namočíme červenú fazuľu do vody izbovej teploty tak, aby bola 2,5 cm ponorená, s 1 ČL (5 ml) soli aspoň na 30 minút alebo do použitia.
2. V ďalšej strednej mise namočíme celé perzské sušené limetky do vody izbovej teploty na 30 minút alebo do použitia; na misu položíme tanier, aby boli limetky ponorené.

3. Mäso zo všetkých strán ochutíme 1 ČL (5 ml) soli a 1/2 ČL (2,5 ml) korenia. Vo veľkom liatinovom hrnci alebo hrnci zohrejeme na stredne silnom ohni 1¼ PL (18 ml) oleja alebo ghí, kým sa nezačne lesknúť. Ochutené mäso vložíme do hrnca v jednej vrstve. Opekáme, občas obrátime, kým mäso nie je zo všetkých strán dobre opečené, asi 10 minút. Dierovanou lyžicou preložíme mäso na tanier a odložíme.
4. Oheň stlmíme na stredný, a keď sa vypečený tuk v hrnci začne lesknúť, pridáme cibuľu a opekáme, kým nie je sklovitá a okraje nie sú zlatohnedé, 7 až 10 minút.
5. Opečenú cibuľu posypeme 1 ČL (5 ml) kurkumy, dôkladne premiešame a opekáme, kým nezavoňia, asi 30 sekúnd.
6. Do hrnca nalejeme 590 ml vody, privedieme do varu a pritom zoškrabeme zo dna všetky pripečené zvyšky.
7. Pridáme opečené mäso. Premiešame, znova privedieme do varu, potom oheň stlmíme na stredne mierny, aby sa udržal mierny var; prikryjeme a varíme 30 minút.

8. Medzitým pripravíme bylinky. Všetky čerstvé bylinky a pór alebo pažítku dobre umyjeme. Rozložíme ich na čistú kuchynskú utierku a jemne zrolujeme, aby sme odstránili prebytočnú vodu. Prípadne na to isté použijeme odstredivku na šalát.

9. Zo zväzkov petržlenovej a koriandrovej vňate oberieme listy a najjemnejšie stonky (ak chceme, zvyšky a dlhšie tvrdé stonky si odložíme na iné účely, napríklad na vývar). Všetky čerstvé bylinky (vrátane pažítky alebo póru) nasekáme čo najjemnejšie. Čím jemnejšie ich nasekáme, tým lahodnejší bude ghormeh sabzi. Na sekanie byliniek môžeme pokojne použiť kuchynský robot. Pažítku alebo pór však nikdy nesekáme v kuchynskom robote samostatne — zmenili by sa na nepríjemnú kašovitú hmotu. Buď ich zmiešame s petržlenovou a koriandrovou vňaťou a nasekáme v kuchynskom robote spolu, alebo ich jednoducho nasekáme zvlášť po starom, ostrým nožom na doske.
10. Keď sa mäso varí 30 minút, scedíme fazuľu a pridáme ju do hrnca, premiešame a prikryjeme. Oheň upravíme tak, aby obsah hrnca jemne bublal. Varíme ďalších 30 minút.

11. Medzitým vo veľkej panvici zohrejeme na stredne silnom ohni 35 ml ghí alebo oleja, kým sa nezačne lesknúť. Oheň stlmíme na stredný. Pridáme polovicu nasekanej bylinkovej zmesi. Opatrne premiešame, aby sa dobre spojila s olejom. Opekáme, kým nie je dobre obalená a nezačne sa sťahovať, asi minútu. Pridáme zvyšok nasekanej zmesi petržlenovej vňate, koriandra a póru. Za častého miešania opekáme 10 minút, kým sa nestiahne, potom posypeme rozdrvenými sušenými listami senovky gréckej. Za častého miešania opekáme ďalej, kým bylinky nie sú veľmi zvädnuté a tmavozelené, ale nie pripálené, ešte asi 10 minút. Bylinky sú hotové, keď sú na dotyk trochu suché, ale po pritlačení chrbtom lyžice z nich vystupuje lesklý jasnozelený olej a cítiť silnú pikantnú vôňu. Je to kľúčový krok, ktorý môže trvať spolu 20 až 25 minút. Buďme trpezliví.
12. Celé perzské sušené limetky scedíme. Ostrým predmetom (napríklad hrotom vidličky alebo špičkou ostrého noža) urobíme do šupky každej limetky 6 alebo 7 malých dierok.

13. Keď sa mäso varí 1 hodinu, pridáme k nemu opečené bylinky a prepichnuté sušené limetky a jemne premiešame. Prikryjeme, oheň podľa potreby upravujeme, aby sa udržal jemný var, a varíme, každých 20 minút jemne premiešame, kým mäso a fazuľa nie sú mäkké a ragú nezhustne, 60 až 80 minút.

14. V tomto čase by mali byť celé perzské sušené limetky už dosť mäkké, nafúknuté a šťavnaté — plné kyslastej, trpkej, zemitej tekutiny. Dierovanou lyžicou alebo malým sitkom vyberieme jednu limetku a veľmi jemne ju zatlačíme chrbtom vidličky tak, aby sa šupka neporušila, a necháme časť tekutiny zvnútra odkvapkať do ragú. Zopakujeme s ďalšími 3 alebo 4 limetkami. Hrncom jemne zakrúžime. Ochutnáme. Ak necítime dostatok kyslastej, trpkej, zemitej chuti limetiek, zopakujeme so zvyšnými limetkami. Nevadí, ak sa pri tom šupka limetiek poruší — len dáme pozor, aby sa do ragú nedostali semienka, pretože pri žuvaní trochu horknú.

15. Hotový ghormeh sabzi má byť dosť hustý, veľmi tmavozelený, s červenou fazuľou, kúskami mäkkého mäsa a limetkami vykúkajúcimi z mora zelených byliniek, s výrazne kyslastou chuťou a jedinečnou vôňou varenej senovky gréckej, ktorá naplní celú kuchyňu. Podľa potreby dosolíme a podávame.

cat.en: Canned beans can replace the dried beans: add them during the last 30 minutes of cooking. Some Persian, Afghan and Middle Eastern markets sell frozen or dried ready-mixed ghormeh sabzi herbs.

en.v: The strained lamb broth can be refrigerated for up to 2 days with the lamb shanks in it to keep them moist; remove any solidified fat on the surface before rewarming and separating shanks from broth. If making this for your family and not for a large gathering, you can assemble individual plates and avoid preparing the large serving platter; this will make it easier to store and reheat leftovers.

sk.v: Precedený jahňací vývar môžeme uchovávať v chladničke až 2 dni aj s jahňacími kolenami, aby zostali šťavnaté; pred ohriatím a oddelením kolien od vývaru odstránime stuhnutý tuk z povrchu. Ak varíme pre rodinu, a nie pre veľkú spoločnosť, môžeme pripraviť jednotlivé taniere namiesto veľkej servírovacej misy; zvyšky sa tak ľahšie uchovávajú a ohrievajú.

c.t: Shrak or markook flatbreads vary in size and thickness; very thin pocketless Lebanese pita or good flour tortillas can replace them, and the bread can even be skipped. Use enough torn pieces to cover the serving platter completely.
Toast the almonds in a dry stainless-steel skillet, tossing often; in a moderate oven, stirring occasionally; or in the microwave.

Placky shrak alebo markook sa líšia veľkosťou aj hrúbkou; nahradiť ich môže veľmi tenká libanonská pita bez vrecka alebo kvalitné pšeničné tortilly a chlieb môžete aj vynechať. Natrhaných kúskov použite toľko, aby úplne zakryli servírovací tanier.
Mandle opražte na suchej nerezovej panvici za častého premiešavania, v stredne vyhriatej rúre za občasného miešania alebo v mikrovlnke.

en.t: 4 lamb shanks (about 1500 g total)
1 medium (226 g) yellow onion, peeled but left whole
10 allspice berries
5 cardamom pods
4 cloves
3 bay leaves
1 cinnamon stick
1 tsp (3 g) Diamond Crystal kosher salt; for table salt use half as much by volume or the same weight
One (1000 g) Tetra Pak of liquid jameed, such as Kasih and Ziyad, or 1 disc of jameed (roughly 226 g) soaked overnight in 473 ml water and then blended until smooth
453 g full-fat plain yogurt (preferably goat or sheep, but cow milk works as well)
1 tbsp (10 g) cornstarch
Kosher or sea salt
1 tbsp (15 ml) extra-virgin olive oil
8 medium cloves garlic, crushed or minced
566 g jasmine or Calrose rice
2 tbsp (30 ml) unsalted butter or ghee
2 tbsp (30 ml) extra-virgin olive oil
1/2 tsp (1.5 g) Diamond Crystal kosher salt; for table salt use half as much by volume
1/4 tsp (1.2 ml) turmeric
1 large shrak, markook, or other thin flatbread
113 g slivered almonds, toasted until golden

1. For the Broth: In a large pot or Dutch oven, cover the lamb shanks with enough water to barely submerge. Set over medium-high heat and cook just until water comes to a boil and foam rises to the surface. Remove from heat, drain shanks, then wash with water to remove any foam clinging to them.

2. Wash pot well, then return the shanks to it along with the onion, allspice, cardamom, cloves, bay leaves, cinnamon, and salt. Add enough water to cover all the ingredients by 2.5 cm. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce heat to maintain a simmer and cook until shanks are very tender but not falling off the bone, 1 1/2 to 2 hours.
3. Transfer shanks to a platter and keep warm. Strain broth, discarding solids; keep warm. Wash pot once more.

4. Meanwhile, for the Yogurt Sauce: In a small saucepan, whisk together liquid jameed (or reconstituted jameed), yogurt, cornstarch, and 118 ml water. Season with salt. Bring to a boil over medium heat, whisking constantly, then remove from heat (it is very important to whisk continuously to prevent curdling; if it does curdle, use a handheld immersion blender to bring it back together into a smooth sauce). The sauce should be relatively thick at this point, almost like a pureed vegetable soup.

5. In a small skillet, heat olive oil and garlic over medium heat until garlic is fragrant and cooked through, but not at all browned, about 2 minutes. Pour the garlic and its oil into the yogurt and stir to combine. The sauce should be quite salty and sour, so add salt as needed.
6. For the Rice: In a medium mixing bowl, rinse rice in several changes of cold water until water is almost clear, then cover rice with cold water and let soak for 15 minutes. Drain well.

7. In a large nonstick pot or Dutch oven, heat the butter and oil over high heat until butter is melted. Add rice, stirring to fully coat in the oil, then add 710 ml water along with the salt and turmeric. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer and cook, uncovered, until most of the water has been absorbed, 2 to 5 minutes. Stir once, then carefully cover pot with a clean kitchen towel and cover tightly with the lid. Remove from heat and let stand 15 minutes.

8. To Assemble and Serve: Pour 1000 ml of the strained broth into the cleaned large pot or Dutch oven along with the yogurt sauce. Whisk to form a very smooth sauce (if it isn't smooth, use an immersion blender to smooth it out). The sauce should have a consistency somewhere between whole milk and half-and-half; if it's too thick, whisk in more broth, 15 ml at a time, until proper consistency is reached. Season once more with salt, if necessary, bearing in mind the sauce should be very salty and tangy, almost like a very strong feta cheese.

9. Add the lamb shanks to the sauce and bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce heat to a simmer and cook until lamb is heated through and the sauce is thick enough to coat the shanks in a thickened and creamy glaze, about 15 minutes. If sauce is still too thin, continue simmering until the sauce reaches a heavy cream–like consistency.

10. To serve, tear up bread into large pieces and arrange on a large, round serving platter in a single, slightly overlapping layer. Pour enough yogurt sauce over the bread to soak through and soften. Fluff the rice, then spoon in a mound on top of the bread. Set shanks on top. Ladle more yogurt sauce all over until it has soaked through the rice and bread (you don't want the mansaf so wet that it begins to flow like soup, but you can be generous with the sauce). Sprinkle all over with the toasted almonds.
11. Serve, passing more yogurt sauce at the table for diners to add to their plates.

c.t: 1. For the Broth: In a large pot or Dutch oven, cover the lamb shanks with enough water to barely submerge. Set over medium-high heat and cook just until water comes to a boil and foam rises to the surface. Remove from heat, drain shanks, then wash with water to remove any foam clinging to them.

2. Wash pot well, then return the shanks to it along with the onion, allspice, cardamom, cloves, bay leaves, cinnamon, and salt. Add enough water to cover all the ingredients by 2.5 cm. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce heat to maintain a simmer and cook until shanks are very tender but not falling off the bone, 1 1/2 to 2 hours.
3. Transfer shanks to a platter and keep warm. Strain broth, discarding solids; keep warm. Wash pot once more.

4. Meanwhile, for the Yogurt Sauce: In a small saucepan, whisk together liquid jameed (or reconstituted jameed), yogurt, cornstarch, and 118 ml water. Season with salt. Bring to a boil over medium heat, whisking constantly, then remove from heat (it is very important to whisk continuously to prevent curdling; if it does curdle, use a handheld immersion blender to bring it back together into a smooth sauce). The sauce should be relatively thick at this point, almost like a pureed vegetable soup.

5. In a small skillet, heat olive oil and garlic over medium heat until garlic is fragrant and cooked through, but not at all browned, about 2 minutes. Pour the garlic and its oil into the yogurt and stir to combine. The sauce should be quite salty and sour, so add salt as needed.
6. For the Rice: In a medium mixing bowl, rinse rice in several changes of cold water until water is almost clear, then cover rice with cold water and let soak for 15 minutes. Drain well.

7. In a large nonstick pot or Dutch oven, heat the butter and oil over high heat until butter is melted. Add rice, stirring to fully coat in the oil, then add 710 ml water along with the salt and turmeric. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer and cook, uncovered, until most of the water has been absorbed, 2 to 5 minutes. Stir once, then carefully cover pot with a clean kitchen towel and cover tightly with the lid. Remove from heat and let stand 15 minutes.

8. To Assemble and Serve: Pour 1000 ml of the strained broth into the cleaned large pot or Dutch oven along with the yogurt sauce. Whisk to form a very smooth sauce (if it isn't smooth, use an immersion blender to smooth it out). The sauce should have a consistency somewhere between whole milk and half-and-half; if it's too thick, whisk in more broth, 15 ml at a time, until proper consistency is reached. Season once more with salt, if necessary, bearing in mind the sauce should be very salty and tangy, almost like a very strong feta cheese.

9. Add the lamb shanks to the sauce and bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce heat to a simmer and cook until lamb is heated through and the sauce is thick enough to coat the shanks in a thickened and creamy glaze, about 15 minutes. If sauce is still too thin, continue simmering until the sauce reaches a heavy cream–like consistency.

10. To serve, tear up bread into large pieces and arrange on a large, round serving platter in a single, slightly overlapping layer. Pour enough yogurt sauce over the bread to soak through and soften. Fluff the rice, then spoon in a mound on top of the bread. Set shanks on top. Ladle more yogurt sauce all over until it has soaked through the rice and bread (you don't want the mansaf so wet that it begins to flow like soup, but you can be generous with the sauce). Sprinkle all over with the toasted almonds.
11. Serve, passing more yogurt sauce at the table for diners to add to their plates.

1. Vývar: vo veľkom hrnci alebo liatinovom hrnci zalejeme jahňacie stehná (kolienka) toľkou vodou, aby boli len tak-tak ponorené. Postavíme na stredne silný oheň a zohrievame, kým voda nezačne vrieť a na povrch nevystúpi pena. Odstavíme z ohňa, stehná scedíme a opláchneme vodou, aby sme odstránili prichytenú penu.

2. Hrniec dobre umyjeme, potom doň vrátime stehná spolu s cibuľou, novým korením, kardamómom, klinčekmi, bobkovými listami, škoricou a soľou. Prilejeme toľko vody, aby boli všetky suroviny ponorené o 2,5 cm. Na stredne silnom ohni privedieme do varu, potom oheň stlmíme, aby sa udržal mierny var, a varíme, kým stehná nie sú veľmi mäkké, ale mäso ešte neodpadáva od kosti, 1 1/2 až 2 hodiny.
3. Stehná preložíme na tanier a udržiavame v teple. Vývar precedíme, pevné zvyšky vyhodíme; udržiavame ho v teple. Hrniec ešte raz umyjeme.

4. Medzitým jogurtová omáčka: v malom kastróliku metličkou zmiešame tekutý jameed (alebo rozriedený jameed), jogurt, kukuričný škrob a 118 ml vody. Osolíme. Na strednom ohni za stáleho šľahania privedieme do varu, potom odstavíme z ohňa (je veľmi dôležité neustále šľahať, aby sa omáčka nezrazila; ak sa zrazí, ponorným mixérom ju znova spojíme do hladkej omáčky). Omáčka by teraz mala byť pomerne hustá, takmer ako zeleninová krémová polievka.

5. V malej panvici zohrejeme na strednom ohni olivový olej s cesnakom, kým cesnak nezavoňia a nie je prepečený, ale vôbec nezhnedne, asi 2 minúty. Cesnak aj s olejom vlejeme do jogurtu a premiešame. Omáčka má byť dosť slaná a kyslá, preto podľa potreby dosolíme.
6. Ryža: v strednej mise preplachujeme ryžu vo viacerých dávkach studenej vody, kým voda nie je takmer číra, potom ryžu zalejeme studenou vodou a necháme 15 minút namočenú. Dobre scedíme.

7. Vo veľkom nepriľnavom hrnci alebo liatinovom hrnci zohrejeme na silnom ohni maslo s olejom, kým sa maslo neroztopí. Pridáme ryžu a miešame, kým sa celá neobalí v oleji, potom prilejeme 710 ml vody a pridáme soľ a kurkumu. Privedieme do varu, potom oheň stlmíme na mierny a varíme bez pokrievky, kým sa väčšina vody nevstrebe, 2 až 5 minút. Raz premiešame, potom hrniec opatrne prikryjeme čistou kuchynskou utierkou a pevne zakryjeme pokrievkou. Odstavíme z ohňa a necháme 15 minút postáť.

8. Skladanie a podávanie: do umytého veľkého hrnca alebo liatinového hrnca nalejeme 1000 ml precedeného vývaru spolu s jogurtovou omáčkou. Metličkou vyšľaháme veľmi hladkú omáčku (ak nie je hladká, vyhladíme ju ponorným mixérom). Omáčka má mať konzistenciu niekde medzi plnotučným mliekom a polosmotanou (half-and-half); ak je príliš hustá, prišľahávame ďalší vývar, po 15 ml, kým nemá správnu konzistenciu. Ak treba, ešte raz osolíme; omáčka má byť veľmi slaná a kyslastá, takmer ako veľmi výrazný syr feta.

9. Do omáčky pridáme jahňacie stehná a na stredne silnom ohni privedieme do varu, potom oheň stlmíme na mierny a varíme, kým sa mäso neprehreje a omáčka nie je dosť hustá na to, aby stehná pokryla hustou krémovou glazúrou, asi 15 minút. Ak je omáčka stále príliš riedka, varíme ďalej, kým nemá konzistenciu smotany na šľahanie.

10. Na podávanie natrháme chlieb na veľké kusy a poukladáme ich na veľký okrúhly servírovací tanier v jednej vrstve, mierne prekrývajúc. Chlieb polejeme toľkou jogurtovou omáčkou, aby sa nasiakol a zmäkol. Ryžu prekypríme a navŕšime na chlieb. Navrch položíme stehná. Naberačkou polievame ďalšiu jogurtovú omáčku po celom povrchu, kým nenasiakne do ryže a chleba (mansaf nemá byť taký mokrý, aby tiekol ako polievka, ale s omáčkou môžeme byť štedrí). Celé posypeme opraženými mandľami.
11. Podávame a pri stole ponúkneme ďalšiu jogurtovú omáčku, ktorú si stolovníci pridajú na taniere.

time.en: not given | Cook: not given | Total: not given

en.t: 235 ml low-sodium chicken broth
1 boneless half leg of lamb (1590–1810 g), trimmed of surface fat
120 ml packed fresh cilantro leaves
5 medium garlic cloves, minced or pressed through a garlic press (about 5 tsp (25 ml))
2 tsp (10 ml) dried thyme leaves
2 tsp (10 ml) paprika
2 tsp (10 ml) ground cumin
Salt and ground black pepper
8 tbsp (115 g) unsalted butter, softened
1 tbsp (15 ml) olive oil

1. Adjust an oven rack to the lower-middle position and heat the oven to 190 °C (fan 170 °C). Set a rack inside a large roasting pan, add the broth to the pan, and set aside. Lay the lamb with the rough interior side facing up (which was against the bone), cover with plastic wrap, and pound to an even 2 cm thickness.

2. Process the cilantro, garlic, thyme, paprika, cumin, 1 tsp (4.5 g) salt, and 1/2 tsp (2.5 g) pepper in a food processor until finely chopped. Add the butter and process until smooth, about 20 seconds.

3. Rub half of the butter mixture over the rough interior side of the lamb, leaving a 2.5 cm border around the edge. Roll and tie the lamb into a compact roast. Pat the roast dry with paper towels and season with salt and pepper.

4. Heat the oil in a 30 cm skillet over medium-high heat until just smoking. Brown the lamb until well browned on all sides, about 2 minutes per side, reducing the heat if the pan begins to scorch. Use tongs to stand the roast on each end to brown, about 30 seconds per end. Melt the remaining butter mixture in a saucepan over low heat or in a microwave on 50% power for 1 minute; set aside.

5. Transfer the browned roast to the rack in the roasting pan and roast until an instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part registers 55 °C (medium-rare), 45 to 55 minutes, basting with the reserved melted butter mixture every 10 minutes. Transfer the meat to a carving board, tent with foil, and let rest for 10 to 15 minutes. Cut into 1.5 cm slices, pour the pan drippings over the lamb and serve immediately.

1. Rošt v rúre posunieme do dolnej strednej polohy a rúru rozohrejeme na 190 °C (teplovzdušnú na 170 °C). Do veľkého pekáča vložíme mriežku, do pekáča nalejeme vývar a odložíme. Jahňacie mäso položíme drsnou vnútornou stranou nahor (tou, ktorá priliehala ku kosti), prikryjeme potravinovou fóliou a vyklepeme na rovnomernú hrúbku 2 cm.
2. V kuchynskom robote nasekáme nadrobno koriandrovú vňať, cesnak, tymián, papriku, rímsku rascu, 1 ČL (4,5 g) soli a 1/2 ČL (2,5 g) korenia. Pridáme maslo a rozmixujeme dohladka, asi 20 sekúnd.

3. Polovicou maslovej zmesi potrieme drsnú vnútornú stranu jahňacieho mäsa, pričom po okraji necháme 2,5 cm voľný pás. Mäso zrolujeme a previažeme do kompaktnej pečienky. Pečienku osušíme papierovými utierkami a osolíme a okoreníme.

4. V 30 cm panvici rozpálime na stredne silnom ohni olej, kým práve nezačne dymiť. Jahňacie mäso opečieme, kým nie je zo všetkých strán dobre opečené, asi 2 minúty z každej strany; ak sa panvica začne pripaľovať, stlmíme oheň. Kliešťami postavíme pečienku na každý koniec a opečieme aj konce, asi 30 sekúnd z každého. Zvyšnú maslovú zmes roztopíme v kastróliku na miernom ohni alebo v mikrovlnnej rúre na 50 % výkonu 1 minútu; odložíme.

5. Opečenú pečienku preložíme na mriežku v pekáči a pečieme, kým vpichový teplomer zapichnutý do najhrubšej časti neukáže 55 °C (medium-rare), 45 až 55 minút; každých 10 minút polievame odloženou roztopenou maslovou zmesou. Mäso preložíme na dosku na krájanie, voľne prikryjeme alobalom a necháme 10 až 15 minút odpočívať. Nakrájame na plátky hrubé 1,5 cm, polejeme výpekom z pekáča a hneď podávame.

en.t: 2 tbsp (30 ml) vegetable oil
6 black peppercorns
4 green cardamom pods
2 black cardamom pods
1 cinnamon stick
1 red onion, halved and sliced thin crosswise
1 tsp (5 ml) grated garlic
1 tsp (5 ml) grated fresh ginger
455 g 90-percent lean ground beef
3/4 tsp (4.5 g) table salt
2 tsp (10 ml) ground coriander

1/2 tsp (2.5 ml) ground turmeric
1/2 tsp (2.5 ml) ground cumin

59 ml whole-milk yogurt

59 ml chopped fresh cilantro, plus extra for garnish

1. Heat oil in medium saucepan over medium heat until shimmering. Add peppercorns, green and black cardamom pods, and cinnamon stick and cook, stirring occasionally, until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Add onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until onion is browned, 7 to 10 minutes.

2. Add garlic and ginger and cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Add beef and salt. Increase heat to medium-high and cook, stirring to break up meat into very small pieces and scraping up any browned bits. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until mixture sizzles and bottom of saucepan appears dry, 7 to 12 minutes longer.

3. Add coriander, chile powder, turmeric, and cumin and cook, stirring constantly, until spices are well distributed and fragrant, about 1 minute. Add tomatoes; yogurt; and chile, if using, and cook, stirring frequently, until tomatoes release their juice and mixture begins to simmer, about 2 minutes. Adjust heat to maintain gentle simmer. Cover and cook, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes have broken down and wooden spoon scraped across bottom of saucepan leaves clear trail, 12 to 18 minutes. Stir in cilantro and season with salt and pepper to taste. If desired, remove cinnamon stick and cardamom pods. Transfer to serving bowl, garnish with extra cilantro, and serve.

c.t: 1. Heat oil in medium saucepan over medium heat until shimmering. Add peppercorns, green and black cardamom pods, and cinnamon stick and cook, stirring occasionally, until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Add onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until onion is browned, 7 to 10 minutes.

2. Add garlic and ginger and cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Add beef and salt. Increase heat to medium-high and cook, stirring to break up meat into very small pieces and scraping up any browned bits. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until mixture sizzles and bottom of saucepan appears dry, 7 to 12 minutes longer.

3. Add coriander, chile powder, turmeric, and cumin and cook, stirring constantly, until spices are well distributed and fragrant, about 1 minute. Add tomatoes; yogurt; and chile, if using, and cook, stirring frequently, until tomatoes release their juice and mixture begins to simmer, about 2 minutes. Adjust heat to maintain gentle simmer. Cover and cook, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes have broken down and wooden spoon scraped across bottom of saucepan leaves clear trail, 12 to 18 minutes. Stir in cilantro and season with salt and pepper to taste. If desired, remove cinnamon stick and cardamom pods. Transfer to serving bowl, garnish with extra cilantro, and serve.

1. V strednom kastróliku zohrejeme na strednom ohni olej, kým sa nezačne lesknúť. Pridáme zrnká korenia, zelené a čierne struky kardamónu a škoricu a za občasného miešania opekáme, kým nezavoňajú, asi 30 sekúnd. Pridáme cibuľu a za občasného miešania opekáme, kým cibuľa nezhnedne, 7 až 10 minút.

2. Pridáme cesnak a zázvor a za stáleho miešania opekáme, kým nezavoňajú, asi 30 sekúnd. Pridáme hovädzie mäso a soľ. Oheň zvýšime na stredne silný a opekáme, mäso miešaním rozdrobíme na veľmi malé kúsky a zoškrabeme pripečené zvyšky. Za občasného miešania opekáme ďalej, kým zmes nezačne prskať a dno kastróla sa nezdá suché, ešte 7 až 12 minút.

3. Pridáme koriander, čili prášok, kurkumu a rímsku rascu a za stáleho miešania opekáme, kým sa koreniny dobre nerozložia a nezavoňajú, asi 1 minútu. Pridáme paradajky, jogurt a čili papričku, ak ju používame, a za častého miešania varíme, kým paradajky nepustia šťavu a zmes nezačne mierne vrieť, asi 2 minúty. Oheň upravíme, aby sa udržal jemný var. Prikryjeme a za občasného miešania varíme, kým sa paradajky nerozpadnú a drevená varecha ťahaná po dne kastróla nezanecháva čistú stopu, 12 až 18 minút. Vmiešame koriandrovú vňať a dochutíme soľou a korením. Ak chceme, vyberieme škoricu a struky kardamónu. Preložíme do servírovacej misy, ozdobíme ďalšou koriandrovou vňaťou a podávame.

cat.en: Break up the meat well as it browns and let the liquid cook off fully before adding the spices, so the keema tastes rich, not boiled.
cat.sk: Mäso pri opekaní dobre rozdrobte a tekutinu nechajte úplne odpariť skôr, ako pridáte korenie, aby keema mala plnú chuť a nechutila ako varená.

tip.en: Add the frozen peas at the end of cooking so they stay as bright green pops of colour.
tip.sk: Mrazený hrášok pridajte až na konci varenia, aby zostal jasnozelený a pridal jedlu farebné bodky.

tip.en: Cut the potato into 1 cm pieces and cook them in the sauce with the tomatoes, so they become tender and soak up the sauce; it's ready when a spoon dragged across the pan leaves a clear trail.
tip.sk: Zemiaky nakrájajte na 1 cm kúsky a varte ich v omáčke s paradajkami, aby zmäkli a nasiakli omáčkou; hotové je to, keď vareška ťahaná po dne zanechá čistú stopu.

en.v: Corned beef can be cooked up to a week before serving. Once cooked, corned beef can be kept, well-wrapped and refrigerated, for about two weeks.

sk.v: Corned beef môžeme uvariť až týždeň pred podávaním. Uvarený, dobre zabalený a uložený v chladničke vydrží asi dva týždne.

en.t: 1 whole flat or point cut beef brisket, trimmed, about 2250 g
100 g Diamond Crystal kosher salt
10 g (about 1 1/2 tsp) pink salt or 7.5 g (about 2 tsp) saltpeter
30 g (about 2 tbsp) packed brown sugar
2 tbsp (30 ml) whole black peppercorns
2 tbsp (30 ml) yellow mustard seeds
2 tbsp (30 ml) whole coriander seeds
1 tbsp (15 ml) allspice berries
6 whole cloves
1 tbsp (15 ml) ground ginger
6 bay leaves, roughly torn
905 g carrots, peeled and roughly chopped
905 g russet potatoes, peeled and roughly diced
1 whole head white or green cabbage, cut into 6 to 8 wedges (905 g–1360 g total)

1. Eight days before serving, combine salt, pink salt (or saltpeter), and brown sugar in a small bowl and whisk until homogeneous. Rub evenly over every surface of brisket. Combine peppercorns, mustard, coriander, allspice, cloves, ginger, and bay leaves and sprinkle evenly over both sides of beef, pressing spices gently into the meat until they stick. Seal the beef in a vacuum sealed bag or a zipper-lock bag with all of the air pressed out of it. Place in the coldest part of the refrigerator and let rest for 7 days, flipping once a day.

2. To Cook in a Sous-Vide Cooker: The day before serving, remove beef from the bag and rinse off all spices under cold, running water. Pat dry with paper towels. Re-seal in a vacuum bag and cook at 80 °C until tender, about 10 hours. Proceed to step 4.

3. To Cook in a Dutch Oven: The day before serving, remove beef from the bag and rinse off all spices under cold, running water. Pat dry with paper towels. Preheat oven to 95 °C (fan 75 °C). Place brisket in large Dutch oven, cover with water by several cm, and bring to a simmer over high heat. Remove from heat, cover with lid slightly ajar, place in oven, and cook until completely tender, about 10 hours. Proceed to step 4.
4. Once beef is cooked, transfer to an airtight container along with cooking liquid. Let rest in refrigerator at least overnight, and up to 3 days.

5. The day of: Transfer cooking liquid to a large saucepan or Dutch oven along with carrots, potatoes, and cabbage. Top up with water until vegetables are submerged. Slice beef thinly against the grain and fan slices out in large skillet. Add 235 ml of liquid from pot to skillet and place skillet on top of pot. Cover skillet. Bring the pot to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a simmer. Cook until vegetables are completely tender and beef is heated through, about 45 minutes. Serve immediately with hot mustard.

1. Osem dní pred podávaním zmiešame v malej miske soľ, ružovú soľ na nakladanie (alebo liadok) a hnedý cukor a metličkou premiešame dohladka. Zmesou rovnomerne potrieme každý povrch hrudí. Zmiešame zrnká korenia, horčicu, koriander, nové korenie, klinčeky, zázvor a bobkové listy a rovnomerne posypeme obe strany mäsa; korenie jemne vtlačíme do mäsa, kým sa neprichytí. Mäso uzavrieme do vákuového vrecka alebo uzatvárateľného vrecka, z ktorého vytlačíme všetok vzduch. Vložíme do najchladnejšej časti chladničky a necháme 7 dní, raz denne obrátime.

2. Príprava v sous-vide hrnci: deň pred podávaním vyberieme mäso z vrecka a pod studenou tečúcou vodou z neho opláchneme všetko korenie. Osušíme papierovými utierkami. Znova uzavrieme do vákuového vrecka a varíme pri 80 °C, kým nie je mäkké, asi 10 hodín. Pokračujeme krokom 4.

3. Príprava v liatinovom hrnci: deň pred podávaním vyberieme mäso z vrecka a pod studenou tečúcou vodou z neho opláchneme všetko korenie. Osušíme papierovými utierkami. Rúru rozohrejeme na 95 °C (teplovzdušnú na 75 °C). Hrudí vložíme do veľkého liatinového hrnca, zalejeme vodou tak, aby bola niekoľko cm ponorená, a na silnom ohni privedieme k miernemu varu. Odstavíme z ohňa, prikryjeme pokrievkou nechanou mierne pootvorenou, vložíme do rúry a varíme, kým nie je úplne mäkké, asi 10 hodín. Pokračujeme krokom 4.
4. Keď je mäso hotové, preložíme ho aj s vývarom do vzduchotesnej nádoby. Necháme v chladničke aspoň cez noc a najviac 3 dni.

5. V deň podávania: vývar prelejeme do veľkého hrnca alebo liatinového hrnca spolu s mrkvou, zemiakmi a kapustou. Dolejeme vodu, aby bola zelenina ponorená. Mäso nakrájame naprieč vláknami na tenké plátky a vejárovito ich rozložíme vo veľkej panvici. Do panvice nalejeme 235 ml tekutiny z hrnca a panvicu postavíme na hrniec. Panvicu prikryjeme. Hrniec privedieme na silnom ohni do varu, potom stlmíme na mierny var. Varíme, kým zelenina nie je úplne mäkká a mäso prehriate, asi 45 minút. Hneď podávame s ostrou horčicou.

cat.en: Cooking the corned beef at a precise low temperature lets the connective tissue turn slowly into gelatin while the meat loses little moisture.
cat.sk: Varenie pri presnej nízkej teplote nechá spojivové tkanivo pomaly sa zmeniť na želatínu, pričom mäso stratí len málo šťavy.
